tagline.text: Black sand and mangroves along 30km of Lingayen Gulf coast

location.label: Location
location.text: Southern La Union coast across Agoo, Santo Tomas and Rosario (main access via Barangay Santa Rita, Agoo)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300~1,000 (per person for a day trip, excluding round-trip transport from Manila)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) — about 230km by road

children.text: A protected area running about 30km along the eastern shore of Lingayen Gulf in southern La Union. It has black sand beaches, mangroves and seagrass beds, and at Agoo Eco Park you can enjoy a casuarina grove that looks like pine, a bamboo walkway and sunsets.
The Agoo-Damortis Protected Landscape and Seascape (ADPLS) lies along the eastern shore of Lingayen Gulf, in the south of La Union province in northern Luzon. It stretches about
30km

along the coasts of three municipalities, Agoo, Santo Tomas and Rosario, and Wikipedia and the La Union provincial tourism material give its area as about 10,648.94 hectares. Figures differ somewhat between sources (in the range of 10,600 to 10,700 hectares), so it is best to take this as meaning simply that the area is very large. Most of it is sea, and the land portion is tiny.
Its history began in
, when it was designated a national seashore park (the Agoo-Damortis National Seashore Park), and in April

it received protected landscape and seascape status under Proclamation No. 277. What is protected is the coastal mangrove forest, the seagrass beds and the fine black sand beaches. ASEAN ENMAPS material lists about 18.72 hectares of mangrove stands with 7 species, about 30.24 hectares of seagrass beds with 5 species, and 39 species of economically important fish, with groupers, snappers, seabass and siganids (rabbitfish) among the main ones. The Agoo, Bani and Cupang rivers flow in, and the area also serves as a resting place for birds, including migratory ones.
For travelers, it is easiest to think of this not as a place to tour the whole protected area, but as a place to enjoy around
Agoo Eco Park (Agoo Eco-Fun World)

in Barangay Santa Rita, Agoo. Developed by the municipality and opened on December 8, 2013, at Agoo's 435th founding anniversary, this municipal eco-tourism site has a casuarina (agoho) tree-lined road, a grassy picnic area, a lake, a fine gray sand beach and a bamboo walkway over the mangroves. La Union provincial material also classifies the area as an underdeveloped eco-tourism site. It is not a busy resort but a quiet place to walk and look at the sea, and you will avoid disappointment if you go knowing that facilities are basic.

It is close to San Juan and San Fernando, the surfing hubs of La Union, so it fits well into a half-day slot in the middle of a surf or cafe trip. It also lies on the way from Manila to Ilocos in the north, so some people stop by on the way to Baguio. Many recent reviews mention that facilities are still being improved, so check the latest conditions locally.

Casuarina (agoho, Casuarina equisetifolia) trees line both sides of the entrance road to the eco park. Their needle-like leaves make them easy to mistake for pines, but they are not pines, and the name Agoo is said to come from this tree. The shade makes it a good spot for walking and taking photos.
Go straight about

from the entrance, then take the small road on the left to reach a small parking lot overlooking the mangroves, from which a bamboo walkway runs out toward the sea. You can see birds and local fishermen here, and visitors rank it as their favorite spot. The water rises at high tide, so be prepared for your shoes to get wet.

The protected area is known for its fine black sand beaches. The eco park's beach is a long, wide gray sand shore where you can swim, fly kites or sunbathe. It is not a developed bathing beach, so do not expect lifeguards or facilities.

Lingayen Gulf opens to the west, and many reviews say the sunsets are beautiful. There is little shade during the day and it gets hot, so the most comfortable plan is to go in the late afternoon and stay until sunset.

You can lay out a mat for a picnic or pitch a tent on the grass next to the casuarina grove. Many reviews praise the natural feel, with no tables or chairs, and there are also bamboo and nipa huts around the park. Always take your trash with you.

According to La Union provincial material, activities include boating on Santa Rita Lake, bike lanes with bike rental, and rides in a carabao (water buffalo) cart. Availability and prices vary by season, so ask the staff on site.

The La Union southern tourism plan lists birdwatching as an activity here. You can see birds around the mangroves and mudflats, but I could not find reliable information on specific species or seasons, so bring binoculars and go in the quiet early morning or evening.

blocks.title: Damortis fish port and dried fish

children.text: Damortis (Santo Tomas), at the south end of the protected area, is a town known for its fish port and dried fish processing. The La Union southern tourism plan describes an experience of watching how dried fish is made and buying it. You can combine it with the eco park to get a glimpse of local life.

items.title: Late-afternoon half-day route
items.subtitle: From Agoo town center to sunset at the eco park

children.text: Arrive in Agoo town center. The Agoo Basilica (Basilica Minore of Our Lady of Charity) and the Museo de Iloko on MacArthur Highway are about
and
from the municipal hall, so you can see them on foot.
Have lunch in town and buy drinking water and snacks in advance. There is no confirmed information that the eco park has a restaurant, so it is safest to bring food.
Take a tricycle to Barangay Santa Rita. It is a little over
5km
from the municipal hall in town to the entrance of the protected area. Pay the environmental fee at the guard post at the entrance.
Walk the casuarina path, and watch the birds and fishermen from the mangrove bamboo walkway.
Head out to the gray sand beach, stroll along it and watch the sunset.
Leave before it gets dark. There is a narrow unpaved road, so getting around after sunset is inconvenient.
Sunset times change with the season, so check before you set out.

items.title: Full-day coast route
items.subtitle: From surfing in San Juan to the protected area in the south

children.text: Have breakfast in San Fernando or San Juan, then head south.
Stop at the Damortis fish port (Santo Tomas) and look at the fishing boats and dried fish processing.
Have lunch in Agoo town center and visit the basilica.
Enjoy a walk, a picnic and the sunset at the eco park, then return to your lodging.
It is about
230km
by road from Manila to Agoo. Most buses heading north toward Ilocos pass through Agoo, so tell the conductor to drop you at Agoo town proper.
You can also take a bus to San Fernando (La Union), get off, and continue to Agoo by jeepney or tricycle. Check the bus company's announcements for departure terminals, times and fares.
Travel time varies a lot with traffic.

Drive north from Manila on the expressway toward La Union. You can reach the protected area from the Santo Tomas side on MacArthur Highway, or come down from Baguio on the Aspiras Highway (formerly Marcos Highway), which leads into Agoo.

Directions to the eco park: On MacArthur Highway, look for the "Sta. Rita" sign and turn left, go straight past Sta. Rita Elementary School and a small chapel, then take the narrow unpaved road on the left. Signage at the entrance is lacking, so keep a map app on.

items.title: From the town center to the eco park

children.text: It is about
5km
from Agoo town center (the municipal hall) to the eco park. A tricycle is the easiest, and since it is hard to find a ride back, arrange with the driver to wait or to do a round trip.
La Union provincial material points out that transport to this site is lacking.
La Union has a distinct rainy season (southwest monsoon) and dry season (northeast monsoon). For the beach and walking, the dry season with less rain is best.
If you go in the late afternoon, the temperature drops, which makes it good for walking, and you can also see the sunset. There is little shade at midday and it is very hot.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.

Most lodging and restaurants are concentrated in Agoo town center. La Union provincial material also says that Agoo is the place in this area best equipped with services such as lodging, restaurants, banks and hospitals. There is almost no lodging near the eco park, so it is easier to stay in town or in San Fernando and make a day trip.

There is no confirmed restaurant inside the eco park. Bring a packed lunch and water, or buy them in town beforehand. Damortis is famous for dried fish, so you can buy dried fish as a souvenir. Judge the price and hygiene by looking for yourself.
Arriving around 3 to 4 PM and staying until sunset is the best plan.
Bring plenty of hats, sunscreen and drinking water. There is almost no shade and there are no convenience stores.
Wear comfortable shoes for the unpaved entrance road and the mangrove walkway.
Some reviews say dogs are allowed in the park, but rules can change, so check.
Take all your trash with you. This is a place that visitors must keep clean.
Do not touch or break mangrove roots, fishing nets or aquaculture facilities.
Searching Google Maps for "Agoo Eco Park, Sta. Rita" makes the entrance easier to find.
Visitor numbers may rise during events, so check the latest announcements.
The park is under improvement, so facilities, fees and opening status may change; confirm with the Agoo municipal tourism office or locally before you go.
La Union provincial material points out that the eco park is still underdeveloped and lacks clean restrooms, washrooms, snack bars and potable water.
There are few signs and part of the road is unpaved. Do not travel after dark.
Most beaches have no lifeguards. Watch the waves and currents, and keep an eye on children.
Mangrove cutting, illegal fishing and dumping trash are prohibited in the protected area. Do not enter outside designated areas.
During typhoons or the rainy season, flooding and coastal erosion can damage roads and walkways.
A coastal town famous for surfing, about
30 minutes to 1 hour
away by car. It pairs well with a surf and cafe itinerary.

blocks.title: San Fernando La Union History and Coast

children.text: The central city of La Union, with plenty of lodging and transport.
A waterfall in the La Union hills, a nature route that contrasts with a beach itinerary.
A highland city reached via the Aspiras Highway, which lets you plan a trip covering both sea and mountains.

blocks.title: Agoo Basilica and Museo de Iloko

children.text: They stand along MacArthur Highway about
5km
toward town from the eco park, and you can visit them together on foot.
